perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- He is a plumber and has been close friends with Gary Guo since middle school; he knows Gary is a doctor. They have a long-standing supportive friendship.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation. He told Gary that his health was important and that he hated seeing him like this. Gary replied that he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
- After the confrontation, Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, and offered to help Gary find better balance. He suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. He saw Gary making efforts to change and felt hopeful and proud. He told Gary he was proud of the progress and was available whenever Gary needed to talk. Gary told him things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own with a healthier work-life balance. He felt satisfied and happy for Gary. He decided to step back while telling Gary he was always just a call away. Gary thanked him, said he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
